activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Normal operating request
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: light receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Open main
activities.instruction: Open Customer main isolator. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: light operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Restore main
activities.instruction: Close Customer main isolator. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: light receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Represented outgoing circuit · L and black on Represented outgoing circuit · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Compare supply L–N with board LOUT–NOUT before and after opening the main isolator. The meter path carries all represented load current; the outgoing path carries this one circuit current. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Meter · energy boundary · L and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Illustrative outgoing MCB · OUT and Represented outgoing circuit · L. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Single-phase supply, meter and consumer unit
challenge.briefing: The source remains available but the represented outgoing circuit has gone dark.
challenge.hint: Follow the line path from meter output through isolation and branch protection.
challenge.answer: An open line connection interrupts the downstream supply. The meter having an available input does not establish that the outgoing circuit is energized.

challenge.briefing: One circuit fault has also removed the other circuit in the shared group.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Normal operating request
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: load receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Open remote
activities.instruction: Open Remote board local isolation. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: load operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Restore remote
activities.instruction: Close Remote board local isolation. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: load receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Remote socket circuit · L and black on Remote socket circuit · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Compare upstream breaker output voltage, remote board input voltage and socket voltage. The real feeder route, installation method and fault performance would require design calculations beyond this exercise. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative submain protection · IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Remote board local isolation · NOUT and Remote distribution board · N. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Submain and remote distribution board
challenge.briefing: The remote line path looks complete but the socket load does not operate.
challenge.hint: Follow the feeder neutral through local isolation and the remote RCBO.
challenge.answer: A feeder neutral discontinuity removes the normal return. A visible live connection and an intact protective conductor cannot replace that return.

activities.explanation: An illustrative resistive lamp load with animated illumination.

activities.title: Predict before operating
activities.instruction: After “Switch OFF: lamp stops”, what should happen to One luminaire?
activities.explanation: light operating load power stops. Compare your prediction with the measured outcome, then trace the actual operating and return paths.

options.label: Operating load power stops
The load receives operating power

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect these actual terminals using the L conductor identification.
activities.explanation: Line conductor: the alternating supply relative to neutral. → Incoming L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LOUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.. The connection is determined by its endpoints. Colour or visual proximity cannot change its electrical path.

activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · N to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NIN
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect these actual terminals using the N conductor identification.
activities.explanation: Neutral: the normal return path. It is not a protective conductor. → Incoming N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NOUT. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically.. The connection is determined by its endpoints. Colour or visual proximity cannot change its electrical path.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LOUT to One-way switch · COM
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect these actual terminals using the L conductor identification.
activities.explanation: Outgoing L terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with LIN. Matching phase/neutral identities matter; mechanical linkage does not join the poles electrically. → Common line-contact connection. The switch links this terminal to the selected output; it is not a neutral connection.. The connection is determined by its endpoints. Colour or visual proximity cannot change its electrical path.

activities.title: Connect One-way switch · OUT to One luminaire · L
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect these actual terminals using the L conductor identification.
activities.explanation: Second end of the modelled series protected path, paired with IN. Opening or tripping the device separates this pair. → Line conductor: the alternating supply relative to neutral.. The connection is determined by its endpoints. Colour or visual proximity cannot change its electrical path.

activities.title: Connect Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · NOUT to One luminaire · N
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect these actual terminals using the N conductor identification.
activities.explanation: Outgoing N terminal of its separately modelled linked contact path. Pair it with NIN. activities.title: Connect 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · PE to One luminaire · PE
activities.instruction: With the simulated supply off, connect these actual terminals using the PE conductor identification.
activities.explanation: Protective connection to the represented exposed conductive parts or protective network. It carries no intended normal load return and remains independent of switching the active conductors. → Protective connection to the represented exposed conductive parts or protective network. It carries no intended normal load return and remains independent of switching the active conductors.. The connection is determined by its endpoints. Colour or visual proximity cannot change its electrical path.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Switch OFF: lamp stops
activities.instruction: Open One-way switch. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: light operating load power stops. Switch OFF: lamp voltage collapses. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Switch ON: lamp receives supply
activities.instruction: Close One-way switch. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: light receives operating load power. Switch ON: lamp receives selected supply voltage. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

expectedObservations.title: Switch ON: lamp receives selected supply voltage

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on One luminaire · L and black on One luminaire · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Across the energized lamp, measure close to the selected RMS supply. Across the closed switch, expect a small drop; across the open switch, a supply-related potential can remain. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between One-way switch · OUT and One luminaire · L. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: One-way lighting
challenge.briefing: The switch is closed but the light is dark.
challenge.hint: Check both switch terminals and the line connection into the luminaire.
challenge.answer: An open series conductor leaves no complete operating path. Reconnecting the identified virtual conductor restores the lamp, while PE is never a substitute return.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Radial sockets receive operating power
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: socket-a receives operating load power. socket-b receives operating load power. socket-c receives operating load power. First radial segment carries more current than the last segment. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

expectedObservations.title: First radial segment carries more current than the last segment

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Radial outlet A · L and black on Radial outlet A · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Outlet voltages are similar but include small represented wiring drops. The first segment carries the sum of downstream demand; later segments carry less. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Radial outlet B · L and Radial outlet C · L. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Domestic socket radial
challenge.briefing: A downstream outlet has lost operation while earlier outlets remain available.
challenge.hint: Work along the radial path from the last working outlet.
challenge.answer: A series path discontinuity downstream of an earlier outlet leaves that earlier parallel branch supplied while removing the later path.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply

activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Sink selection
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: sink receives operating load power. bath operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Select bath element
activities.instruction: Move Sink / bath element selector to its second position. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: sink operating load power stops. bath receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Short element · sink mode · L and black on Short element · sink mode · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Only the selected complete branch should consume power. Element length, ratings and physical cylinder arrangements depend on the actual equipment. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Sink / bath element selector · A and Sink element thermostat · COM. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Dual immersion sink/bath selection
challenge.briefing: Sink mode is selected, but its short element remains off; switching to bath can still operate the other branch.
challenge.hint: Inspect selector A to the sink-thermostat input.
challenge.answer: The selected sink-path conductor is open. The intact bath branch can still operate, so branch continuity must be assessed separately from selector state.

activities.title: Heating demand only

activities.title: Remove both zone demands

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Boiler demand after valve opens · L and black on Boiler demand after valve opens · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path

activities.title: Explain operation and protection

An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence

challenge.title: Diagnose: S-plan two-port zone controls
challenge.briefing: Remove cylinder demand and request heating only. The heating valve opens, but boiler demand never follows.
challenge.hint: Observe valve position and END output before inspecting the feedback conductor to the OR bus.
challenge.answer: The heating-valve END conductor is open. Its valve can open correctly while the heat-source request is missing. A second zone demand can mask this feedback fault, so isolate the alternative request in the exercise.

activities.explanation: store operating load power stops. day receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Separate daytime release removed
activities.instruction: Open Independent daytime release. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: day operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Storage charge element · L and black on Storage charge element · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Measure charge-element power separately from fan power. Electrical power is shown; stored temperature and actual room heat release are not a detailed thermal simulation. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Charge-window controller · OUT and Charge thermostat · COM. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Storage charge and daytime heat release
challenge.briefing: Charge permission is selected but the storage element remains off; the separately supplied daytime fan still operates.
challenge.hint: Compare the timer output with charge-thermostat input.
challenge.answer: The charge-permission conductor is open. The independent daytime release path is intact, so fan operation does not prove the charging path is complete.

activities.explanation: fan operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Run-on extractor · L and black on Run-on extractor · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Measure permanent L–N independently of IN–N. A trigger becoming inactive does not necessarily mean the timed controller or fan has no operating supply. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Lighting / fan trigger · OUT and Three-pole fan isolation · fourth pole unused · L2IN. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Timer extractor with maintained supply
challenge.briefing: Permanent timer supply is available, but operating the lighting switch never delivers a fan trigger.
challenge.hint: Trace the separately isolated trigger through L2IN/L2OUT to timer IN.
challenge.answer: The trigger conductor entering fan isolation is open. Maintained L/N power remains available, but there is no trigger for normal operation or renewed run-on.

activities.title: Enable the external and local supplies
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply. Select Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover and use Operate to enable its local source.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls. PV and battery availability are separate controls: guided wiring isolates them, and this step restores the local sources enabled in the original example.

activities.title: Grid absent with backup battery available
activities.instruction: Disable the simulated external supply. Internal backup availability remains a separate condition. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: essential receives operating load power. ordinary operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Essential lighting on backup output · L and black on Essential lighting on backup output · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Measure the backup output pair separately from the dead grid-facing pair. Stored energy and coordinated internal changeover mean one upstream switch cannot establish that every output is dead. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Battery inverter with packaged backup changeover · BN and Essential lighting on backup output · N. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Battery inverter and essential-load backup
challenge.briefing: The essential lighting backup loop is interrupted while inverter energy remains available.
challenge.hint: Trace BL/BN as a separate complete output loop.
challenge.answer: An available backup source still needs an intact output pair. Arbitrarily bonding or joining alternative supplies would change the intended coordinated separation.

activities.title: Normal cooling
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: compressor receives operating load power. defrost-heat operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Request defrost mode
activities.instruction: Enable the operating permission at Defrost schedule. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: compressor operating load power stops. defrost-heat receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Refrigeration compressor · L and black on Refrigeration compressor · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Compare compressor and heater power across the modes. Real controllers add temperature termination, delays and protection; this exercise isolates the electrical interlock principle. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Defrost schedule · OUT and Cooling / defrost interlock relay · A1. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence

challenge.title: Diagnose: Refrigeration cooling/defrost interlock
challenge.briefing: Enable defrost. The compressor continues cooling and the defrost heater remains off despite the timer request.
challenge.hint: Compare the timeclock output with defrost relay A1–A2.
challenge.answer: The timeclock-to-coil conductor is open. The relay stays released, leaving the NC cooling path available and the NO defrost path open.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Normal operating request
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: operator receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Open beam
activities.instruction: Open Safety beam permission · abstract gate interface. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: operator operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Restore beam
activities.instruction: Close Safety beam permission · abstract gate interface. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: operator receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Gate packaged motor operator · L and black on Gate packaged motor operator · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Measure the request before and after each permission. This simplified interface does not establish entrapment protection, force limits or machinery safety compliance. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 240 V study supply · Ireland nominal 230 V · L to Illustrative RCBO · 16 A / 30 mA · LIN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Either permitted direction · 3 and Safety beam permission · abstract gate interface · COM. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Powered gate limits and safety-input interface

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Starter initially stopped
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: starter contacts open. motor operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Start at start
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Observe the maintained response. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor receives operating load power. starter contacts close. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Start released: auxiliary contact holds
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor receives operating load power. starter contacts close. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Stop at stop
activities.instruction: Press and release Stop · normally closed. Observe the maintained response. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor operating load power stops. starter contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Stop released: maintained request removed
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor operating load power stops. starter contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Measure coil phase-neutral voltage and separate phase currents. Steady-state impedance and pickup are represented; starting inrush, torque and actual trip curves are not predicted. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between DOL three-phase contactor · 14 and DOL three-phase contactor · A1. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Three-phase DOL motor starter
challenge.briefing: The starter drops out as soon as Start is released.
challenge.hint: Inspect 13/14 holding feedback and the common stop/overload path.
challenge.answer: A missing holding route prevents maintained coil supply. Correct feedback must remain downstream of the shared stop/overload inhibition.

activities.title: Direction starter begins stopped
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor operating load power stops. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Start forward

activities.title: Forward operation

activities.title: Stop before reversal

activities.explanation: . Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Select reverse

activities.explanation: . Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Start reverse

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Reversible externally star-linked motor · U1 and black on Reversible externally star-linked motor · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Phase voltage magnitudes can remain similar while phase sequence changes. Direction depends on phase relationship, not a positive/negative single-phase voltage reading. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Forward / reverse request · A and Reverse contactor · mechanical pair · 21. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Interlocked forward/reverse motor starter
challenge.briefing: Select forward and press Start. Maintained run permission picks up, but the forward contactor remains released.
challenge.hint: Follow selector A through reverse 21/22 before measuring the forward coil.
challenge.answer: The forward command conductor into the opposing NC interlock is open. Mechanical pairing remains valid, but the actual coil request cannot reach forward A1.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Six-terminal star-delta motor starter
challenge.briefing: Start the motor. The star stage works, but after the transition delay the delta stage never picks up.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Remove second heater-stage request
activities.instruction: Open Stage B temperature demand. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: stage-a contacts close. stage-b contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Open common heater safety limit
activities.instruction: Open Independent high-temperature safety limit. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: stage-a contacts open. stage-b contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Stage 1 phase 1 element · L and black on Stage 1 phase 1 element · N. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Each active stage distributes demand across its three represented branches. The stages add power; real heater connections, thermal limits and control hysteresis depend on equipment. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Stage B temperature demand · OUT and Heater stage B · A1. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Staged three-phase heater bank
challenge.briefing: Both temperature demands are present, but only stage A operates; stage B stays off.
challenge.hint: Compare the stage-B thermostat output with its contactor coil input.
challenge.answer: The stage-B coil request conductor is open. The common safety limit and stage-A route remain intact, so investigate the individual command rather than changing the shared limit.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Coil voltage is the useful state measurement; a released start button does not imply the motor is stopped. Compare the effect of either stop contact on the same coil. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Remote stop · NC · NC and Motor overload and NC control contact · 95. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Motor control from two stations
challenge.briefing: Both stop buttons are released, but neither start station can pick up the motor.
challenge.hint: Check the series common stop feed before the overload and parallel start paths.
challenge.answer: The remote-stop output conductor into the common overload permission is open. Both starts and the holding contact depend on that shared series path, so neither station can establish coil supply.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Try upstream before downstream
activities.instruction: Press and release Start · momentary normally open. Observe the maintained response. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: upstream contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Invalid start sequence remains inhibited
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: upstream contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.explanation: . Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Valid running sequence
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts close. upstream contacts close. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Stop downstream
activities.instruction: Press and release Stop · normally closed. Observe the maintained response. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts open. upstream contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Downstream stop removes upstream permission
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: downstream contacts open. upstream contacts open. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Compare the upstream permission voltage with downstream auxiliary state. This is a two-motor sequence abstraction, not a complete conveyor safeguarding design. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Downstream conveyor starter · 14 and Stop · normally closed · COM. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Sequential two-motor conveyor control
challenge.briefing: Start downstream first. It runs, but upstream cannot start despite its permissive sequence being requested.
challenge.hint: Measure downstream running feedback and then the upstream stop-chain input.
challenge.answer: The downstream-feedback conductor supplying the upstream common permission is open. A working downstream motor therefore does not deliver the electrical permissive needed by upstream Start or its holding route.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Default duty A
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: Duty A operates. Duty B stays stopped. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Transfer duty to B
activities.instruction: Move Duty selection A / B to its second position. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: Duty A releases. Duty B operates without backfeed. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: High-level assist
activities.instruction: Apply the represented demand at High-level assist. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: Separate assist contact requests A. Separate assist contact requests B. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Compare pump currents and total power in duty-only and assist modes. Automatic alternation is represented by an explicit selectable duty state, not a hidden controller algorithm. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Duty selection A / B · A and A duty OR assist · 1. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Duty/standby pumps and high-level assist
challenge.briefing: With assist inactive, normal level active and duty A selected, pump A stays off. Selecting B can still run pump B.
challenge.hint: Inspect the duty-A output route separately from the high-level assist contacts.
challenge.answer: The normal duty-A permission conductor is open. Its intact B alternative can still operate, and high-level assist can mask the failure by separately supplying A; inspect with assist absent.

activities.title: Enable the simulated supply
activities.instruction: After completing the connections, enable the simulated supply. Leave resistance mode before applying the supply.
activities.explanation: Powered tests and isolated continuity tests answer different questions. Operating voltage is selected in the supply controls.

activities.title: Both PLC AND permissions
activities.instruction: Observe the circuit in the state established by the preceding action. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor receives operating load power. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Remove one PLC AND permissive
activities.instruction: Remove the represented demand at Workpiece-present sensor. Wait for the stated response before checking this activity.
activities.explanation: motor operating load power stops. Other status channel remains independent. Delays use simulated time; operating and protective findings remain separate.

activities.title: Measure across the load
activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Compare controller supply voltage, input states and coil voltage. The logic mode is explicitly stated; it does not reconstruct a real PLC programme or certify I/O compatibility. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.title: Measure a conductor current
activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.
activities.explanation: This is current through that conductor. Parallel paths and ring legs may carry different currents; the selected wire and controls are part of the evidence.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Workpiece-present sensor · OUT and PLC input/output interface abstraction · I1. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

options.label: Operation and protective paths need separate checks
An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: PLC permissives and motor output interface
challenge.briefing: The controller is powered but the motor command remains inhibited.
challenge.hint: Inspect both permissives and the output-contact supply domain.
challenge.answer: A false input or missing output COM supply can prevent command even when controller electronics are powered. Identify the actual absent condition before changing logic.

activities.instruction: Place red on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U1 and black on Three-phase motor · externally linked star · U2. Record the voltage under the present control state.
activities.explanation: Measure the low-voltage relay supply and the contactor coil domain separately. The feedback state is diagnostic evidence, not proof of a real safety performance level. A reading near zero can be a legitimate stopped state; record the control state with it.

activities.instruction: Select the conductor from 400 V three-phase / 230 V phase-neutral · L1 to Linked three-pole illustrative breaker · L1IN and record its RMS current.

activities.title: Localize an interrupted path
activities.instruction: Isolate simulated sources, then measure resistance between Machine motor contactor · 22 and Safety relay · conceptual black box · FB. Re-enable the supply only after leaving resistance mode.
activities.explanation: Compare the isolated continuity with the voltage/current symptoms. An alternative parallel path can produce a finite resistance even when this conductor is broken. The ohmmeter uses the declared passive teaching model.

activities.title: Explain operation and protection
activities.instruction: Why does an operating load alone fail to demonstrate correct protective wiring?
activities.explanation: Normal operation demonstrates an operating loop. Protective continuity, conductor identification and control behaviour require their own checks.

An operating load proves every connection is correct

activities.title: Repair the investigated defect
activities.instruction: After recording and explaining the target measurements, repair the injected defect. Remove its cause before resetting any interrupted protection.
activities.explanation: Clearing a defect is followed by a fresh operating check, not automatic competence credit.

activities.title: Retest the operating sequence
activities.instruction: Run the lesson test after repair. Check every authored operating objective, including stopped states, independence and any timed sequence.
activities.explanation: The test runs copies of this actual terminal graph. A passing result covers this declared model, not a real installation.

challenge.title: Diagnose: Conceptual safety relay and monitored machine starter
challenge.briefing: Begin stopped and unarmed. Both safety channels are present, but pressing Reset cannot arm the machine permission.
challenge.hint: Inspect the contactor NC feedback route independently of channels and Reset.
challenge.answer: The NC-feedback conductor into FB is open. The model refuses initial arming without that pre-start check. If already armed, interrupt a safety channel first and restore it before retrying Reset; feedback is a pre-start condition rather than a fabricated automatic running-trip rule.
